prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

U0067: A particular control method might be momentarily infeasible due to the work situation the crew are facing.
U0068: For example, crew might experience a brief communication outage with their remote teammates, physical hand control might be prevented when crew hands are occupied with task work, or existing audio conversations among the team might preclude or interrupt the activation of voice control commands.
U0069: Ultimately, if an advanced informatics display is to be used and found useful by crew, the display and control system must be capable of coping with the complexities of the jobs that crew will face in future operational scenarios.
U0070: For more detail on the Joint AR project, please see Refs: [10, 11].
U0071: Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 18 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations 4 Framing the Scenarios This document prioritizes the deliberate articulation of future work domain attributes and potential corresponding solutions to demands faced by users in those hypothetical situations.
U0072: In doing so, aspects of the envisioned world problem challenges summarized below can begin to be addressed [16]. • plurality: there are multiple versions of how the proposed changes will effect the character of the field of practice in the future. • underspecification: each envisioned concept is vague on many aspects of what it would mean to function in that field of practice in the future; in other words, each is a simplification, or partial representation of what it will mean to practice when that envisioned world becomes concrete. • ungrounded: envisioned concepts can easily be disconnected or even contradict, from the research base, the actual consequences of the changes on people, technology and work. • overconfident: advocates are miscalibrated and overconfident that, if the systems envisioned can be realized, the predicted consequences and only the predicted consequence will occur.
U0073: These challenges all stem from many people having internalized assumptions about what a future system is and what it could and should do.
U0074: In an attempt to help build a common vision for what the future work could look like, this document implements the approach shown Figure 4.1.
U0075: We acknowledge that there is a boundless set of options that might exist one day.
U0076: To cope with the limitless possibilities, we encourage the deliberate construction of a finite set of imagined futures to help narrow the discussion.
U0077: As discussed in Section 4.1, this method is an attempt to overcome some of the initial challenges of the envisioned world problem. use case narratives and momentary demands provide a deliberate set of specific instances that address plurality, underspecification, and ungrounded concerns.
U0078: Providing interface prototypes that trace directly to momentary de- mands provide a mechanism to help address being overconfident by calibrating user expectations to meet the moment in question.
U0079: These efforts should be coupled with iterative prototype testing of a real-world solution help build alignment with system expectations and capabilities within the work domain being built.
U0080: Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 19 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations Figure 4.1: Visual description of the translation of an infinite amount of hypothetical work domain possibilities to a more concrete set of concrete work domain possibilities Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 20 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations DISCLAIMER The framing described here depends on a highly iterative refinement and should serve as a means by which a group of people can imagine in a common direction.
U0081: Agreement and discussion should be iteratively assessed on the use case narratives, momentary demands, and user interface prototypes.
U0082: This approach is not meant to serve as a standalone method but rather demonstrate how to start the process of understanding envisioned user needs and iteratively discover potential solutions as documented in existing human-centered design processes [5, 6]. 4.1 Methods and Approach for Eliciting Advanced Informatics Features 4.1.1 Use Case Definition Template Figure 4.2 shows the components of the use cases defined in this document.
